newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran to tender Hengam gas-condensate development.
newsitem.headline: Iran to tender Hengam gas-condensate development.

text.p: Iran has attracted interest from European and Australian firms to develop the offshore Hengam (Henjam) gas-condensate field which Iran shares with Oman, an Iranian energy official was reported as saying on Monday.

"We are now preparing to call an international tender for development of the (Hengam) oilfield and so far some European and Australian companies have voiced readiness to take part in the tender," said Seyed Jalilian, the director of the offshore division of the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC).
Jalilian's comments were carried by the official Iranian news agency IRNA.
Hengam, which is owned 80 percent by Iran and 20 percent by Oman, had gas reserves of 523 billion cubic meters and 120 million barrels of oil, Jalilian said.
Once developed, Hengam would produce 200-250 million cubic meters of gas daily and 20-25,000 barrels per day of "liquefied oil and gas."

Under the Iran-Libya sanctions act signed by U.S. President Bill Clinton last August, non-U.S. firms that invest $40 million or more an year in the two countries' oil and gas sectors can vulnerable to a range of U.S. trade penalties.

Iran offered international firms the chance to invest in 11 Iranian oil and gas projects in 1995 under the so-called "buy-back" arrangement under which investors would be repaid from crude oil produced at the field being developed.
So far France Total SA and Malaysia's Petronas are the only foreign firms directly developing Iran's oil and gas fields at the Sirri offshore development.
Jalilian described as "satisfactory" the status of talks with foreign firms on developing "buy-back" projects.

Australia's Novus Petroleum Ltd is the operator of the gas-condensate field on the Omani side of Hengam, where production is averaging some 4,000 bpd of condensate, 1,200 bpd of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), and 40 million cubic feet a day (1.1 million cubic meters) of gas.
Iran, the world's third largest oil exporter, produces 3.6 million bpd of crude oil.
